shorts.title: Would Earth Fly Away Without the Moon?
shorts.question: If the Moon vanished, would Earth be thrown out of its orbit?
shorts.hook_text: No Moon. Does Earth fly away?

lines.text: If the Moon vanished tonight, would Earth go flying off into space?
Earth and the Moon circle a shared balance point. It sits inside Earth, about four thousand seven hundred kilometers from the center.
Each month, Earth loops around it at only about twelve meters per second.
Our speed around the Sun? Nearly thirty kilometers per second.
So without the Moon, that little loop just straightens out. Our orbit barely changes.
The real changes are slower, and stranger. The full story is on our channel: The Moon Vanishes Tonight.

shorts.title: Tides Without the Moon
shorts.question: Would the tides stop if the Moon disappeared?

lines.text: Delete the Moon, and the tides... don't actually disappear.
The Sun pulls on the oceans too, with about forty-six percent of the Moon's tidal force.
So tides would shrink to roughly a third of their typical size.
No more spring tides or neap tides. And high water would arrive at nearly the same time every day.
The strip of shore between high and low water would narrow, and the life that depends on it would lose ground.
And tides aren't even the biggest change. Watch the full video to see what is.

shorts.title: The Moon Steers Our Seasons
shorts.question: What keeps Earth's tilt, and our seasons, steady?

lines.text: The Moon is quietly holding our seasons steady. Here's how.
Earth's tilt is what gives us seasons. Today it only rocks between about twenty-two and twenty-four and a half degrees.
The Moon drives about two-thirds of the slow wobble of Earth's axis.
Without it, a 1993 study found the tilt could wander chaotically, from near zero to about eighty-five degrees.
A 2011 study found narrower swings, about ten to twenty degrees. Still enough to redraw the world's climate zones.
Either way, the Moon is a hand on the steering wheel of our seasons. Full story on our channel.
